transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-06
Start time: 09:31 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (recording available)
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lena Ortega (CISO, Ironwood), Markus Veldt (Head of Platform), Priya Shah (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Reviewed Ironwood's SOC 2 / ISO posture and evidence onboarding approach.
- Discussed Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO mapping, audit log retention, and KMS/HSM integration options.
- Agreed to share SOC2 report and schedule technical deep-dive for KMS and VPC/private deployment integration.

Topics: Trust Center access, SOC 2 Type II report, ISO27001 summary, RBAC and SSO mapping, audit logs and retention, KMS/HSM, data residency (EU), evidence handoff timeline.

Action items (captured in meeting): see metadata list.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samira here from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:00:07] Lena (Ironwood CISO): Hi Samira, Lena here. Markus and Priya are with me.
[00:00:11] Markus (Ironwood): Morning.
[00:00:12] Priya (Procurement): Hi all.
[00:00:14] Evan (Redwood SE): Evan here, glad to join.
[00:00:18] Samira: Great. Goal for today is a posture review — get you access to the Trust Center, walk through what evidence we can provide for SOC 2 and ISO, and talk through RBAC/SSO and KMS flows. Anything to add?
[00:00:27] Lena: That sounds right. Main constraints: EU data residency for some workloads, need KMS integration with our HSM for key control, and we want a clean control mapping to our internal matrix for the audit.
[00:00:40] Samira: Perfect, that'll frame the conversation. Quick housekeeping — I'll drop the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO snapshot after the call and invite you to the Trust Center. The technical bits Evan will cover.

[00:00:55] Evan: Cool. I'll start with the Trust Center and evidence surface area. So, Redwood's Trust Center hosts our SOC 2 Type II report, ISO27001 cert summary, control mappings, and audit logs access. Access is role-based — AE/SE invite gets view-only links and audit artifacts. Note, sometimes the transcriber says 'trust tuner' — it's Trust Center.
[00:01:17] Markus: How granular is the RBAC? We want separation between Platform engineers and Security.
[00:01:22] Evan: We support RBAC with predefined roles and custom roles. Platform engineers can be given 'runner' or 'ops' roles with no access to the audit reports, while Security gets 'compliance' role with read access to SOC/ISO artifacts. You can also tie this to SSO via SAML/SSO — we support IdPs like Okta, Azure AD.
[00:01:38] Lena: For SSO, we'd want SCIM provisioning and group sync. Is SCIM supported?
[00:01:44] Evan: Yes — we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. There are a couple of pitfalls to be aware of: attribute mapping for groups needs to match your internal group names, and we sometimes see folks mis-map 'env' groups as 'enviro', so watch for that.

[00:02:05] Priya: From procurement side, we'll need to see the SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary, plus contract language about data residency and encryption at rest.
[00:02:12] Samira: Absolutely, Priya. We'll include residency language samples and our standard KMS/HSM integration appendix.

[00:02:20] Lena: Can you clarify how keys are handled if we want Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) or use an HSM in our cloud tenant?
[00:02:26] Evan: Sure. We have three common patterns: 1) Hosted keys managed by Redwood KMS for hosted customers, 2) Customer-managed keys in their cloud KMS where we use keywrap APIs, and 3) Hardware-backed HSM in VPC/private deployment where the customer controls the master key. For BYOK we do key-wrapping and you can rotate the wrapping key on your cadence.
[00:02:48] Lena: And audit logs around key usage? We need cryptographic operation logs for the auditors.
[00:02:53] Evan: We can surface KMS access logs and key use events via the Trust Center; for Dedicated/Private installs we forward detailed HSM/KMS audit logs to your logging endpoint (Syslog/CloudLogging) with configurable retention. Small caveat: for hosted KMS we retain logs per our retention policy, which we'll share.

[00:03:12] Markus: Regarding data residency — we run in EU and we must ensure embeddings and raw prompts don't leave region for certain datasets. Can Redwood pin workloads to EU-only hosts?
[00:03:21] Evan: Yes, we support region pinning. You can route requests to EU-only model shards and we provide region-specific model variants. The runtime can also be deployed as Private in your VPC for full control. There's a tradeoff: private/VPC gives you isolation but adds ops and cost.
[00:03:36] Samira: We'll include a cost sketch for Dedicated vs Private versus Hosted with region pinning in follow-up.

[00:03:44] Lena: For the control mapping: we'll need to map our controls to Redwood's controls for SOC 2. Do you have a template?
[00:03:49] Evan: Yes, we have a control mapping spreadsheet that maps our control IDs to common frameworks (SOC 2 CC, ISO27001 Annex A). We'll push a starter mapping; you'll edit to show where Ironwood is responsible vs Redwood. Note: the auto-transcript may say 'sea of controls' — it's 'CIS controls' sometimes misheard.

[00:04:10] Priya: If we request SOC 2 evidence, what's the delivery process? PDF attachments, Trust Center links?
[00:04:15] Samira: Typically Trust Center links with time-limited access. For vs auditors, we can provide signed PDFs and allow your external auditors view access for the period of the review.

[00:04:25] Markus: Any concerns about the KV cache or prompt caching from privacy perspective? I saw in docs you have prefix caching, is that isolated?
[00:04:31] Evan: Good callout. We have KV/prefix caching to accelerate inference; for private data you can opt out of caching or enable strict per-tenant isolation. The cache is logically segregated by tenant ID. Transcript note: sometimes 'K-V cache' was transcribed 'K-V cash', so just flag it.

[00:04:50] Lena: For the auditors we need a list of logs — admin activity, model deployments, access changes, and data access to logs. Can you enumerate retention windows?
[00:04:58] Evan: Yes — default retention for audit logs is 180 days on hosted; we offer extended retention as an add-on (1, 3, 7 years). For Dedicated and Private you control retention via your logging pipeline. We'll include a table in the follow-up.

[00:05:12] Samira: Let's talk about a few redlines we commonly see: 1) Data residency—we'll show region pinning language; 2) KMS and key control — BYOK option; 3) Right to audit — we offer auditor access via Trust Center. Anything else?
[00:05:24] Lena: SSO session length and provisioning lifecycle — we need to certify de-provisioning processes.
[00:05:29] Evan: We support SCIM de-provisioning and have session token TTL controls; we can provide the de-provisioning runbook and logs showing group changes.

[00:05:40] Priya: On procurement, what SLAs are available if we go Dedicated vs Hosted?
[00:05:45] Samira: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and a committed throughput profile. Hosted is best-effort but with usage-based pricing. We'll attach the SLA matrix.

[00:05:54] Lena: For private deployment — if we go private in our VPC, what parts of the control scope remain with Redwood vs with Ironwood?
[00:06:00] Evan: In Private, Redwood provides the control plane software and operational guidance; network, KMS HSM, and underlying host hardening are customer-managed. The control mapping shows shared responsibilities; we'll mark each control as R, C, or S (redwood/customer/shared) in the spreadsheet.

[00:06:18] Markus: Can you demo the Trust Center UI quickly? I mostly care about how evidence is organized and how auditors get temporary access.
[00:06:24] Samira: We can do a UI walkthrough but I think that's better in a short screen-share session. For now, Evan can describe the hierarchy.
[00:06:30] Evan: Sure — Trust Center is organized by report type (SOC, ISO), then by control families. Each control has evidence artifacts (policies, screenshots, logs, config exports). You can generate auditor links scoped to a report and time window.

[00:06:46] Lena: Is there an activity log showing who viewed what within Trust Center?
[00:06:50] Evan: Yes, we have audit trails for Trust Center access. Every issuance of an auditor link, and each artifact view is logged with timestamp and subject.

[00:07:00] Priya: Pricing question — do you have an enterprise pack for compliance that includes extended retention and Trust Center premium?
[00:07:05] Samira: Yes, we offer a compliance add-on that bundles extended log retention, dedicated support channel, and Trust Center premium. I'll include pricing examples.

[00:07:16] Markus: For the tech deep-dive, we want Evan to show key rotation flow and how the key wrapping works end-to-end — can you include a flow diagram?
[00:07:24] Evan: Absolutely. I'll prepare a one-page flow (key creation, wrapping, rotation, rotation proof) and bring it to the deep-dive.

[00:07:33] Lena: One more — do you publish a SOC 2 gap remediation plan or previous audit findings? We want to see whether there were any issues and how they were addressed.
[00:07:40] Samira: We include an executive summary of past findings and remediations in the Trust Center; sensitive details are redacted but we provide enough context for auditors.

[00:07:50] Priya: Ok that helps. From next steps standpoint, we'll expect the reports and Trust Center invite, and to schedule the deep-dive. Procurement will review SLA and residency language once received.
[00:07:59] Samira: Great. We'll send the SOC 2 Type II and ISO snapshot by Friday. Evan will schedule the tech session. Anything else before we wrap?
[00:08:07] Markus: No, that's it from Platform.
[00:08:09] Lena: Nothing else. Thanks.
[00:08:11] Samira: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and the calendar invite.
[00:08:16] Evan: Thanks everyone.
